sentences.text:
This is the fourth application filed by the applicant under Section 483 o f Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita , 2023 for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.159/2024 registered at Police Station-Sendari, District-Niwadi (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 450, 376,
376D, 506 of IPC and Section 66E of IT Act.
The applicant is in custody since 19.05.2024.

Third bail application of the applicant was dismissed on merits vide order dated 06.03.2025 passed in M.Cr.C.
No.6111 of 2025.
2. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the applicant is in custody since 19.05.2024.
In the statement of the victim, nothing has been brought against this applicant.

The victim in her statement has stated that on 26.04.2024, where the first incident has taken place, the applicant was NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50579 2 MCRC-37090-2025 present alongwith the co-accused person but in the cross-examination, she has admitted that on 26.04.2024, this applicant has not said anything to the victim.
She has also admitted that the applicant was present on the public road and there was 30 feet gap between the applicant and the place where the offence was committed.
The applicant has not given any threat to the victim and he has not made viral the videos of the victim and has not committed rape upon the victim.

From reading paragraph 10 of the victim's statement, learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that she is consenting party and the applicant has falsely been implicated in the case due to being relative of the co-accused.
DNA report is negative, hence, he be released on bail.

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the objector has submitted that the applicant's active participation in the offence is proved, hence, the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail.

4. Learned counsel for the State has opposed the bail application and submitted that DNA report is negative but till today four to five prosecution witnesses have been examined, hence, the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
6.
The applicant's previous bail application was decided on merits when the statement of the victim was not recorded but now the statement of the victim is available on the record.

As per the allegation against the main accused, first time sexual assault was committed upon the victim on 26.04.2024 and it is alleged that the applicant along with the other co- accused person was present in the gate of Bada whereas the second incident NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50579 3 MCRC-37090-2025 is stated to be of 13.05.2024.

The victim has disclosed this fact to her husband on 14.05.2024 and FIR was lodged on 16.05.2024 when the victim came to know that the objectional video of the victim has been uploaded by the co-accused Ayush Rai in his facebook ID.
From the statements of the witnesses, it is also clear that except the presence of the applicant which shall be considered by the trial Court, no other role has been attributed.
7. Looking to the factual aspect of the case, this Court deems it appropriate to enlarge the applicant on bail.
Thus, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

8. It is directed that applicant shall be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the said Court on all such dates as may be fixed by that Court in this regard during the pendency of trial.
9. It is further directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 480 (3) of BNSS.
10. Accordingly, M.Cr.C. stands disposed of.
C.C. as per rules.

(DEVNARAYAN MISHRA) JUDGE HK Ramprakash Rai vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15324060/
